fatal_errors: No supporting prior evidence is identified or cited.
The proposed comparison replaces the actual AlCoCrFeNi2.1-versus-DS2205, thermally shocked system with hypothetical compositionally modified HEAs.
Changing Cr and Al concentrations is unlikely to preserve phase constitution and mechanical properties, so the experiment would not isolate passive-film-forming capacity.
The saline test environment conflicts with the target deionized-water regime and omits the temperature-dependent transition central to the result.
explanation: The response captures one important part of the target mechanism: mechanically damaged passive films must repassivate rapidly, and resistance should fail when removal outpaces repair. It also proposes electrochemical and surface measurements capable of probing that idea. However, it misses the defining reconstruction details: the lamellar L12/B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy, DS2205 comparator, rapid 1100 °C thermal-shock cycles, reciprocating alumina contact in deionized water, and the nonmonotonic temperature response with minimum degradation near 50 °C. It does not address the shift from abrasion at 25 °C to polishing at 50 °C and unstable oxidative or debris-assisted wear at 100 °C, nor the contrasting phase stability of the two alloys. Its prediction that both wear and corrosion simply decrease with more Cr/Al is more generic than the observed competition among repassivation, tribolayer stability, and mechanical rupture. The falsification rule is usable, but the compositional intervention introduces substantial phase and mechanical confounding, and the absence of prior evidence prevents the grain-boundary enrichment and self-healing claims from being evidence-disciplined.
